title: Case Book: When a Paper Temporary License Takes Over From the License on File
content:
This case book, for the **Driver Services Agreements and Account Standing** product, applies the license takeover rule. The rule fixes the day from which a Wayfare driver's paper temporary license is counted, and so changes the temporary license acceptance days, the calendar days from the upload day for which the temporary license is accepted as the driver's license on file.

## License takeover rule

- When the driver's license expiry date on the agreement is later than the upload day, the temporary license takes over when that license ends, so its cover is counted from that expiry date and the days from the upload day to it are added.
- When the license on the agreement expired at least 14 calendar days before the upload day, the cover is counted from the upload day and the uncovered days beyond 14 are taken off, at most 10 days.
- When it expired fewer than 14 days before the upload day, or on the upload day itself, the cover is counted from the upload day and nothing is added or taken off.

The expiry date read is the driver's license expiry date on the agreement before the upload.

## Cases (hypothetical, upload day 2026-08-10)

| Case | License expiry date on the agreement | Position against the upload day | Days added | Days taken off |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 2026-08-25 | 15 days later | 15 | 0 |
| 2 | 2026-08-10 | the upload day itself | 0 | 0 |
| 3 | 2026-07-31 | expired 10 days before | 0 | 0 |
| 4 | 2026-07-27 | expired 14 days before | 0 | 0 (no days beyond 14) |
| 5 | 2026-07-20 | expired 21 days before | 0 | 7 |
| 6 | 2026-06-30 | expired 41 days before | 0 | 10 (27 days beyond 14, limited to 10) |

In case 4 the license expired exactly 14 days before, so the cover is counted from the upload day; the uncovered days beyond 14 are none. In case 6 the uncovered days beyond 14 are 27, and the most taken off is 10.
